items.summary: my first startup and first love @netlify is refounding for the ai age with some very impressive growth stats despite a low aeo ranking. really impressed by @biilmann who has led the company through so…
items.body:
my first startup and first love @netlify is refounding for the ai age with some very impressive growth stats despite a low aeo ranking. really impressed by @biilmann who has led the company through some tough days but never gave up (unlike me) and is coming out the other end with a much stronger business.

always grateful to Netlify for giving me my first big break as a technical writer/speaker, but wow this kind of tenacity you need to be a decade+ founder in tech piloting a ship while pivoting adroitly is 99.99% percentile in people i have ever come across in the valley

questions i would have ask (behind paywall probably but eh):
1. why arent they using vercel/chatgpt sites/ant artifacts/cloudflare?
2. how does the spend breakdown?
3. how do accounts grow for these nontechnical builders? is there graduation risk (only once bill gets >$1k i get serious about auditing)

quote.text:
Last week, Netlify enjoyed its first day with 100,000 new signups, most of them new to AI and building software.

After taking 5 years to reach 1M users, Netlify doubled to 10M by this past January, and expects to reach 25M by year's end 👀

comments.text:
I think it shows that AEO tracking is actually really hard.

I obviously don't know Render and Railway's numbers, but my guess is that we're onboarding more new users coming from LLM recommendations per day, than they are.
comments.text_zh:
我觉得这说明 AEO 追踪其实非常难。

我显然不知道 Render 和 Railway 的数字，但我猜我们每天通过大模型推荐进来的新用户，比他们还多。

comments.text: I'm on #2 and #3 of that list: Railway for almost all our projects, Vercel for my own apps. Netlify growing like this from #8 shows the ranking isn't everything
comments.text_zh: 我属于那份名单上的第2和第3：我们几乎所有项目都用 Railway，我自己的应用用 Vercel。Netlify 能从第8名这样往上爬，说明排名并不代表一切

comments.text: Paywall is removable for free subscribers (I call it a soft paywall) but this is more detail than what I got. Good questions.
comments.text_zh: 付费墙对免费订阅者可以去掉（我称之为软付费墙），不过这里的细节比我拿到的还多。问题问得好。

comments.text:
Telling detail: growth "despite a low AEO ranking," meaning how often AI assistants suggest you.

If coding agents pick where apps get deployed, that ranking becomes the sales funnel.

Growing without it hints at headroom.
comments.text_zh:
一个说明性的细节：增长是「尽管 AEO 排名很低」，也就是 AI 助手有多经常推荐你。

如果编程智能体会选择应用部署到哪里，这个排名就会变成销售漏斗。

没有它也能增长，暗示还有上升空间。

comments.text: Wait were you part of the founding team of Netlify?
comments.text_zh: 等等，你是 Netlify 的创始团队成员吗？

comments.text: Curious how they plan to handle stateful agent runtime sandboxes at the edge, or if they’re strictly sticking to stateless short-lived serverless.
comments.text_zh: 好奇他们打算如何在边缘处理有状态的智能体运行时沙箱，还是会严格坚持无状态、短生命周期的 serverless。

comments.text_zh: 这么低的 AEO 排名是 Netlify 2027 年最好拿的成绩，我们就是做这类路线图的 https://t.co/Lbenzs1PDC

comments.text: The graduation risk usually hits when generative workloads outgrow edge timeouts and need persistent compute or heavy websocket streaming for agent loops.
comments.text_zh: 毕业风险通常出现在生成式负载超出边缘超时、需要持久算力或为智能体循环做大量 websocket 流式传输的时候。

items.body:
the fact that nobody with decisionmaking power saw this coming a mile away and vetoed the 6.2 astra ad is my primary critique of the astra launch

the model itself is solid minor version improvement guys, efficiency is one of the three most impt RL objectives rn and they are world leading here!!! i am daily driving astra and it is the best workflow automation model i’ve used, no longer getting stuck in horrible loops and efficiently learning thru compactions and skill writing. it’s running a lot of our content publishing pipeline for @latentspacepod and @aiDotEngineer and we wouldnt have nearly the revenue efficiency (>1m/employee) that we have as a bootstrapped business without it

quote.text: @stevekrouse Yeah but your framing is already better than what's in the ad. The ad shows people who are totally disengaged from their work having a panic attack at the moment an authority figure arrives, then slopping out something that they neither care about or understand.

comments.text: Spot on re: efficiency as a first-class RL objective. Curious about one ablation from your daily driving🤔 — if you keep context compaction on but disable/hide the self-written skills, do the bad loops come back? My hunch is compaction does most of the heavy lifting to clear
my critique is that I can't test it because I don't have any usage
Reset?
Astra is much better than Opus / Fable at certain things, particularly workflows and computer use. It also isn't nearly as righteous as Claude.

the efficiency objective is the one that compounds. in agent work the bill isn't really the model, it's the agent restating its own plan and regenerating prose across tool calls. i compressed that layer locally and it moved more than swapping models did
funny how the ad got more reviews than the model he-he
Agreed. In @AlexFinn's test Astra finished in about a third of the time, at about a third of the price. For agent loops that run 50 steps, that difference adds up fast.

The ad critique lands, but the efficiency point is the bigger story. If a small team can run at over $1M per employee because it is cheap to run, that changes what a bootstrapped team can attempt. Efficiency is a feature users feel, even if they never see the RL objective.

items.summary: devin bots are multi-agent teams done right: - always on, proactive (but tuned for ROI) - own outcomes not tasks (but can collab w others) - manages teams of subagents (and reviews itself) - available…
items.body:
devin bots are multi-agent teams done right:
- always on, proactive (but tuned for ROI)
- own outcomes not tasks (but can collab w others)
- manages teams of subagents (and reviews itself)
- available everywhere (call text slack whatever hello @interaction)
- consistent reporting thru interactive artifacts aka devinapps not long chats (HTML is all you need™ @trq212)

this is the preview that @walden_yan gave at AIE. i've been trialing them for a week and i've been able to hand over my AEO, QA, cross-platform app porting, personal admin automation, and video editing work (also simultaneously moving from local agent worktree hell to cloud because ofc this is all cloud based thank god)

hyped concepts this replaces:
- /goal
- "ultracode" / "ultra mode"
- "loop engineering"
- "agent to agent"
- "agent swarms"
- AI employees (see below)

my main aha moment is that you don't want "AI Employees", we do not have agi yet and you will just fail if you overpromise/overexpect. what you want is the "just" the next level of abstraction above single tasks, and the overwhelming consensus I've had talking to everyone at the frontier of agents (yes incl cog competitors) is agent managers that own outcomes.

incidentally, as an employer of humans it's also how i distinguish between someone who "has agency" (owns a problem area, finds issues and researches/brings solutions not problems) and who doesn't (only does precisely what i asked, not proactive, doesn't come up with suggestions i didn't think about). guess which one i value more lol.

if youre a startup, reminder that Devin for Startups offers 65k in credits. apply via clanker

quote.text:
Meet Devin Bots.

From writing firmware to merging thousands of PRs a week, a Devin Bot leads a team of agents to get the job done.

comments.text: "Own outcomes, not tasks" and "collab with others" get hard once every engineer brings their own agent. A bot running its own subagents is a different problem from my Cursor agent and your Claude Code agent seeing the same work and handing it off without a person in between.
who decides the outcome was hit? if the bot closes the ticket but the customer still sees the bug, does it reopen on its own?

An outcome is only owned if someone else can check it was reached. For agent managers, that means each result comes with a record of which subagents did what, what was tested and where a person signed off. Agency without that record is hard to delegate to.
Outcomes over tasks is the right line. Once an agent owns a number, someone still has to own the agent. That part doesn't automate.
The ending is understated and confident, and I think that's why it sticks. It leaves room for you to feel something afterward.
An agent that owns a goal and reports back is much more useful than one that just completes tasks. Proactive help is good only if it saves real time. That is the kind of system I would want.

This is the multi-agent pattern I've been waiting for. Own the outcome, not the task, and report back in something I can actually read instead of a chat log. The teams that hand over real work first will learn fastest.

After a week with Devin Bots, which workflow actually stopped needing your attention, versus just moved your work into review? That distinction seems more useful for the ROI claim than how many subagents are running. QA and video editing may have very different answers.
cool until five autonomous bots refactor the same auth config at 3am

For agents that stay on for weeks, the thing I'd check is whether a correction lasts: if I tell it once not to touch the billing code, the subagents it starts next week should get that rule too. Self-review helps only if it checks the work against those corrections.

comments.text: Thanks for doing the scale math. And if $2,000 a kilo really drops to $200, a lot more small hardware teams get to fly.
comments.text_zh: 感谢你做了规模上的计算。而如果每公斤 2000 美元真能降到 200 美元，那会有更多小型硬件团队有机会飞上天。

comments.text: operations tempo is the constraint now. doesn't matter if you can reuse it if turnaround kills your economics. that's the hard part
comments.text_zh: 现在真正的制约是运营节奏。就算你能复用，如果周转时间拖垮了经济性，那也没用。这才是最难的部分

translation.summary: 作为参照，那是一枚 52 米/171 英尺/15 层楼高的巨型火箭在空中翻转，然后着陆准备复用 预计将把有效载荷发射成本从每公斤 2000 美元降至每公斤 200 美元。可复用性或许是我们有生之年太空飞行中最重要的进步……而且前景里居然还有几匹该死的马在跑，就为了让画面更史诗一点，哈哈

comments.text: 100k already?? That's insane
comments.text_zh: 已经 10 万了？？太疯狂了

comments.text: Congrats. Best conference! 🤘🏻
comments.text_zh: 恭喜。最棒的会议！ 🤘🏻

comments.text: which part got the most questions in chat? curious if people are still stuck on context files or have moved on to reviewing what the agent wrote
comments.text_zh: 聊天里哪一部分问题最多？很好奇大家是还卡在上下文文件上，还是已经转到审查代理写出来的东西了

comments.text: Practices beat landscape for us too. 45 days of two founders + coding agents on telecom tools: what mattered wasn't the model, it was ~6,800 automated tests and a human sign-off before anything public. Any talks on evals outside pure software?
comments.text_zh: 对我们来说，实践同样比全景扫描更重要。两个创始人加上编程代理，用 45 天做电信工具：真正重要的不是模型，而是大约 6800 个自动化测试，以及任何对外发布前的人工签字。有没有纯软件之外、关于评测的分享？

comments.text: coding agent practices is the one I'd watch. would love a segment on what agents get wrong on security by default, like putting keys client side because it "works"
comments.text_zh: 编程代理实践是我会看的那一期。很希望能有一段讲代理在安全上默认会犯哪些错，比如把密钥放在客户端，就因为这样“能跑”

comments.text: Coding agent content is undefeated right now.
comments.text_zh: 编程代理内容现在简直无敌。

comments.text: i run a one-person company with agents doing the building. what i'd love covered is the failure side, cost blowups and what to do when an agent confidently breaks something. any day planned on that?
comments.text_zh: 我一个人开公司，建造工作交给代理做。我很希望能讲到失败的一面，比如成本爆炸，以及代理很自信地把东西搞坏时该怎么办。有安排哪一天讲这个吗？

comments.text: Practical agent talks give viewers something to try after the stream, which seems like a useful signal beyond reach. Do you track which sessions lead people to reproduce a workflow or return with implementation questions? That could help choose the next deep dive.
comments.text_zh: 偏实践的代理分享能让观众在直播结束后有东西可试，这似乎是比曝光量更有用的信号。你会追踪哪些场次会让人去复现一个工作流，或带着实现问题再回来吗？这有助于选择下一次深挖的方向。

comments.text: Do these practical sessions get most of their views live, or do the replays do the heavy lifting?
comments.text_zh: 这些实践场次的播放量，主要来自直播，还是回放在扛大头？

comments.text: Live wins here because agent practices go stale in weeks; a writeup from last month already describes a different set of tools. Would love a segment on failures too, watching an agent go wrong live teaches more than another polished demo.
comments.text_zh: 直播在这里更合适，因为代理实践几周就会过时；上个月的一篇总结描述的已经是另一套工具了。也很希望有一期讲失败，看着代理现场出错，比又一场打磨过的演示更有收获。

translation.summary: 另外，第一天的直播以有史以来最快的速度突破了 10 万观看。讲编程 Agent 的实践与格局，依然是我们做过最强的形式，也是我做过的、产品市场契合度最高的方向，没有之一。https://t.co/cM43xYQLMT
